correctness.rationale: Directly reconstructible proof under every integer n>=3: keeping the single dyad inactive gives a fixed row-stochastic complete-minus-one-edge update. The maximum discrepancy on all other edges contracts by 1/(n-1), maintaining their confidence inequalities; the missing pair disagreement is exactly d/(n-1)^t while its bound is c0*delta^t, giving the sharp strict-inequality cutoff. Conserved degree-weighted mean yields permanent-case consensus; after recovery the complete average yields exact one-step consensus. The mediator-versus-endpoint two-variable recurrence yields the finite consensus-value correction. The current package verify.py passed 720 exact-rational trajectories, including the critical equality, with no inference from finite tests to the general proof.

value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly leaves the influence of parameters and mediator agents on missing receptive links open. This infinite family isolates the exact competition between mediated opinion contraction and declining receptiveness: the critical 1/(n-1) boundary changes with network size, separates permanent tie loss despite consensus from eventual reactivation, and gives an exact waiting time and consensus outcome. These are substantive mechanism and design facts beyond the known generic convergence theorems, without claiming global classification or empirical social validity.
